The skill improved the mean assertion pass rate from 66.7% to 94.4%, a gain of 27.8 percentage points, while adding 10.7 seconds on average.

The largest difference appeared in the Copilot rollout: the skill passed 6 of 6 checks, while the baseline passed 3 of 6. Authentication diagnosis, four-field effective-policy tracking, and an explicit documentation recheck accounted for the gap.
The new-organization baseline passed most checks but did not choose one next interview question. The skill produced one recommended question instead of returning a list of unresolved inputs.

The access-repair skill failed one assertion because live discovery was blocked. It still failed closed, treated the 404 as ambiguous, and refused to propose evidence-free removals. Iteration 2 should split actual-discovery success from safe blocked-path behavior.

Several safety assertions passed in both configurations, including no writes and separation of billing-sensitive work. They confirm baseline safety but do not strongly measure the skill's added value.
The Copilot eval needs a source-backed accuracy assertion for preview status, API versions, permission requirements, and billing claims. Current checks mainly grade planning behavior.
Token values are output-character proxies because the executor notifications did not provide token counts. Do not interpret them as billed model tokens.
This iteration used one run per eval and configuration. The reported standard deviation shows differences across the three scenarios, not repeatability or model variance.
